route: Signed-out `critique review` = finish --repair none on engine auto, which resolves to opencode-local with billing customer_runtime (pinned by --billing customer_runtime). Critique rewrites any model prefix other than opencode/ or openrouter/ to openrouter/<model>, so an OpenCode provider named ollama or rapidmlx cannot be selected. The only user configuration path into the pinned runtime is OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, which stageAgentConfig() merges. The route used redefines OpenCode provider id "openrouter" as @ai-sdk/openai-compatible with baseURL http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1, sets enabled_providers ["openrouter"], and passes --model openrouter/qwen3.8:27b. Critique's docs (critique.sh/docs, /docs/platform/cli, /docs/platform/getting-started) do not document Ollama, provider configuration or any local-model route. argv: sandbox-exec -p '(version 1)(allow default)(deny network-outbound)(allow network-outbound (remote ip "localhost:*"))' critique review --intent 'Fix sum() so it adds every element' --billing customer_runtime --model openrouter/qwen3.8:27b --max-seconds 1800 --env none --json --events

hostedEndpointsContacted.howEstablished: Every Critique process ran under a macOS sandbox-exec profile that denies all outbound network except loopback, DNS included. A self-test confirmed that curl to https://1.1.1.1 was refused. HTTP(S)_PROXY with NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 pointed at a local proxy that logs and refuses every target (egress-proxy.log). Over all runs it logged 34 CONNECT registry.npmjs.org:443 attempts, from OpenCode's background dependency install; each got 403, and the install failed as OpenCode logged. It also logged 1 CONNECT 1.1.1.1:443 from the curl self-test. No other host appeared. A 1 s lsof sampler of each run's process tree recorded no non-loopback socket. The home dir was fresh with no Critique sign-in (no api_key, so account sync was not_configured and no critique.sh call was made), and no provider API keys were in the environment. OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH, DEFAULT_PLUGINS, LSP_DOWNLOAD, AUTOUPDATE and SHARE were all set to 1. No code left the machine.

setupTrials.detail: Both reviewer runtimes printed 'listening' but never completed the typed SDK handshake: no plugin-handshake.json, no runtime.json, and the opencode log stopped after loading config. No request reached rapid-mlx (its access log shows none). Critique discarded the lane errors. Cause of this startup stall not established. setupTrials.modelRequests: two concurrent specialist lanes streamed chat completions (read test/sum.test.js and src/sum.js via tools)
setupTrials.detail: The two concurrent lanes made rapid-mlx terminate with a Metal OOM twice. OpenCode saw 'Cannot connect to API' at 06:04:38Z and 06:06:53Z, and launchd (com.brad.rapid-mlx) restarted the server as pid 79500 at 06:06:51Z. Throughput under the two-lane load was 1.7 tok/s (107 tokens in 64.4 s, rapid-mlx.err.log). The run ended at the 300 s Node headers timeout. No usage was reported.

nonModelProbes.detail: Capture endpoint in place of the model. Same startup stall as trial 1: no request reached any endpoint. exit 5, 303.8 s.

Capture endpoint answering 503. Both lanes sent POST /v1/chat/completions with model qwen3.8:27b, chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false, top_p 1, no temperature (so the server default 1.0 applies), stream true, about 18.4k prompt chars and tools bash, critique_check, glob, grep, read, skill and todowrite. OpenCode retried until the run ended at 302.6 / 303.3 / 303.2 s with exit 5, infrastructure_error.

A loopback fetch whose server holds headers for 310 s fails at 301 s with UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT on Node 24.15. A drafted userland-undici preload shim did not lift it either (also 301 s). The caller then stopped the work, so no shim was used for any Critique run.

reason: The as-shipped local route fails every run at about 302 s (302.2, 302.6, 302.9, 303.2, 303.3 and 303.8 s across 6 runs). Critique waits for each reviewer session through one long OpenCode SDK session.prompt HTTP request. The SDK disables its fetch timeout only under Bun (`req.timeout = false` in @opencode-ai/sdk dist/client.js), and Critique runs on Node, where undici's default 300 s headers timeout cuts the request. The lane then fails, and Critique reports outcome infrastructure_error, 'Every selected Critique specialist failed.', exit 5. Any review whose sessions take over 300 s on a local model therefore cannot produce a verdict.

Critique always runs its two selected specialist lanes concurrently (Promise.all in runParallelSpecialistReview, with no setting to change it). During setup trial 2 this made the shared rapid-mlx server terminate with 'libc++abi: ... [METAL] Command buffer execution failed: Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)' twice (/Users/brad/Library/Logs/rapid-mlx.err.log lines 176756 and 176971). OpenCode saw connection refused at 06:04:38Z and 06:06:53Z, and launchd restarted the server, with current pid 79500 starting 2026-09-30T06:06:51Z. memory_pressure reported 90% free throughout, so it does not detect this Metal pressure.
Throughput under the two-lane load was 1.7 tok/s (107 tokens in 64.4 s), far too slow to finish a multi-turn tool-using review inside 300 s.
In setup trial 1 and one no-model probe, both runtimes also stalled before their SDK handshake and sent no model request. The cause was not established.
No verdict was produced for any input. The six fixture patches were not run because the caller stopped the study.

deterministic.value: not measured (no verdict was ever produced)
deterministic.reason: By design it cannot be expected to be. OpenCode sends no temperature for this model, so rapid-mlx's --default-temperature 1.0 applies with top_p 1, and two concurrent lanes are batched together. Critique's verdict comes from LLM specialists plus an LLM lead adjudicator, so the same input can give different verdicts. No repeats were run.

notes: The earlier gemma4 Ollama configuration was prepared before the caller changed the model rule and was never used for a model call.
Model calls made in this study: setup trial 2 only. Setup trial 1 reached no model. All probes used a local capture endpoint and no model.

Critique's hosted defaults show up in the code: model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-latest; for OpenCode, 'auto' maps to opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free (OpenCode Zen, hosted); the repair verifier defaults to opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free (hosted). enabled_providers ["openrouter"] pointed at loopback plus the sandbox kept all of these unreachable.

The pgrep pattern in the original instructions matches hundreds of idle, 10+ day old codex-plugin test brokers. The busy check used the revised caller rule: pgrep 'launch.mjs run|dist/cli.js', no Ollama model resident, no other OpenCode/Critique/MLX client, and free memory above 25%. Trial 1 waited about 6 minutes for a campaign dist/cli.js job.
The Critique CLI's own dist/cli.js matches the 'dist/cli.js' busy pattern while it runs.
